name: An Enchanting Lesson

angles.text: Scholarly mages often scoff at subterranean vermin, yet Kitta Firewind reminds them that even primitive creatures can reveal unexpected truths about raw magical currents.
Studying at the Tower of Azora in Elwynn Forest gives Alliance adventurers insight into academic wizardry and the surprisingly magical pests infesting their lands.

faq.answer: Kitta Firewind, an enchanter at the Tower of Azora in Elwynn Forest, offers this lesson to adventurers. She teaches that scholarly theory and hands-on practice belong together.
faq.q: Who gives the quest An Enchanting Lesson?

faq.answer: The Tower of Azora stands in eastern Elwynn Forest. It is a bastion of magical study and wizardry amid the farmlands and woods of the human kingdom.
faq.q: Where is the Tower of Azora located?

faq.answer: Kobolds have no formal schooling or scholarly traditions, yet geomancers have an instinctive knack for binding basic cantrips and enchantments into crude wax effigies.
faq.q: How do kobolds know how to use magic?

faq.answer: Crude Wax Effigies are primitive items fashioned by kobold geomancers. Though unsophisticated, they hold bound magic that can be unraveled and studied through disenchanting.
faq.q: What are the wax effigies used for?

faq.answer: Luminous Residue is the essence obtained by deconstructing and disenchanting the crude wax effigies carried by kobold geomancers. It is tangible proof of their innate cantrips.
Kitta Firewind teaches that theoretical knowledge and practical experimentation are inseparable. She urges students to study practical magic wherever it appears.
faq.q: What is the main takeaway of Kitta Firewind's lesson?

sections.body: Kitta Firewind, an enchanter at the Tower of Azora, challenges apprentice enchanters to look beyond polished libraries. She asks them to examine magic where it appears naturally. Even the uneducated kobolds beneath Elwynn Forest channel cantrips into everyday talismans, proof that magical instinct can thrive without formal schooling.
sections.title: Theory and Practice

sections.body: Kobold geomancers shape Crude Wax Effigies with simple folk enchantments. Students obtain the effigies and carefully unravel their bound magic through disenchantment, extracting Luminous Residue. By taking these primitive charms apart, they learn how raw magic behaves in the field. Enchantment's fundamental threads are found through observation as well as in grimoires.
sections.title: Primitive Cantrips

summary: At the Tower of Azora in Elwynn Forest, Kitta Firewind gives An Enchanting Lesson to apprentice enchanters. Kobold geomancers bind simple magic into crude wax effigies, showing why practice matters alongside arcane theory.
